sentences.text:
Applicant :- Afsar Ali
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rakesh Kumar Agrahari,R.K Singh Gaharwar,Rajrshi Gupta,Ram Jata Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Satish Solanki Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The second bail application has been filed on behalf of applicant in Case Crime No.81 of 2018 arising out of S.T. No.486 of 2018, under Sections 498A, 304B, 302, 120B IPC, and Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Madrak, District- Aligarh, with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.

The first bail application has been rejected vide order dated 05.12.2018 passed in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No.42631 of 2018.

Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No.42631 of 2018
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It is submitted that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is also submitted that the informant, namely, Wajid Ali who happens to be the father of the deceased, Shahrun lodged the first information report on the basis of suspicion.
No demand of dowry was ever made by the applicant with him or his daughter.
The applicant never treated the deceased with cruelty.

He also submitted that the co-accused persons, namely, Sarfuddin @ Lehtu and Bablu have been granted bail by coordinate Bench of this Court vide orders dated 06.12.2018 & 08.01.2020 passed in Afsar Ali vs State Of U.P. on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198769750/
1 Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos.45979 of 2018 & 12281 of 2018 respectively after rejection of the first bail application of the applicant.

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that the present applicant is languishing in jail since 17.03.2018 having no criminal history and that in case he is released on bail,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in trial.

Per contra, the learned Additional Government Advocate has opposed the prayer for grant of bail and submitted that the applicant is husband of the deceased who died due to firearm injury and some other witnesses have corroborated the prosecution version.
As per the status of the trial, P.W.9 & P.W.10 have been examined and trial is at its logical end.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of allegations and gravity of offence, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the opinion that no case for grant of bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby rejected.

Trial court is directed to expedite the trial and all endeavours be made to conclude the trial expeditiously preferably within a period of four months after receipt of the certified copy of this order without granting unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties subject to full co-operation by the applicant.
Any observation made above shall not be treated as any finding on the merit and shall not prejudice the trial.

Order Date :- 17.5.2023 SP/-
